name: Breakdown-Fork
note: Deliberately-curated fixtures (LIN-830) for the session-fit fork in lib/prompts/meta-prompt-template.js — multi-phase structure whose phases independently land / genuinely span sessions must read as a `breakdown` signal EVEN ABSENT an explicit "needs multiple sessions" verdict or a formal dependency-arrow plan. Origin dogfood: an autopilot landed LIN-826 (a real 2-phase task) by routing straight to `implementation`, working only Phase 1, then blocking for a human gate instead of decomposing first. POSITIVE (FIX-830-pos) = the REAL LIN-826 description text as the recommender saw it — captured BEFORE its later '## Committed Implementation Plan' section added arrows/verdict — i.e. two prose phases (Phase 1 Harbour wiring with its own Acceptance; Phase 2 autopilot adoption with its own separate Acceptance), no formal arrows, no explicit session-fit verdict -> expect `breakdown`. NEGATIVE (FIX-830-neg) = the overfit trap: a genuinely single-session task whose plan merely LISTS two sequential steps that land together as one PR/close-out (step-listing is NOT phases) -> must stay `implement`. The gate must flip the positive to breakdown WITHOUT regressing the negative or any existing fixture. Inverse failure (over-recommend breakdown on description keyword-saturation) is tracked as LIN-838 — the negative guards against introducing a counting heuristic. Each is a childless In-Progress leaf (no children/focusedChild) so the descent terminates on it.

issue.title: Push-based inter-session communication: event-driven subscriptions replace up-chain polling
issue.description:
## Goal

A **universal, reliable, push-based method for inter-session communication.** When a session emits an event (it reaches a terminal/stopping point), any **subscriber** is woken with a follow-up carrying that event — instead of the subscriber polling for it. The autopilot (and anything else that coordinates sessions) uses this instead of internal polling.

One-line: **replace the up-chain poll with a reliable follow-up.**

## Status — runner half already landed (LIN-827)

The `simple-dispatcher` primitives this depends on **shipped in** [LIN-827](https://linear.app/linearviewer/issue/LIN-827) **and are live in the running dispatcher** (backward-compatible, opt-in — dormant until used):

* **Queue-when-busy:** a follow-up to a busy parent is no longer failed (`reject: session-busy` → `[failed]`). With the opt-in `queueIfBusy` flag it is left unclaimed and delivered on a later poll once the parent reaches its hold. Fan-in serialises for free.
* **Hold budget extended to \~60 min** (`FOLLOWUP_HOLD_MS`, env-overridable); the hold re-arms on every child event and the `--resume` fallback catches anything past the cap.

So the **hold + push delivery + queue** are all in place. What remains is **Harbour** (detect child terminal → enqueue a parent-addressed follow-up; pass the flags) and the **autopilot** (stop polling, trust the push). The runner needs no further change for V1; the true liveness-anchor (decision #4) stays deferred to the parallel-execution track.

## Why (evidence: [LIN-824](https://linear.app/linearviewer/issue/LIN-824/research-agent-wait-latency-audit-where-does-the-wall-clock-go-when))

The [LIN-824](https://linear.app/linearviewer/issue/LIN-824/research-agent-wait-latency-audit-where-does-the-wall-clock-go-when) wait-latency audit found the runtime is correct but slow, and the slowness is one structural asymmetry:

* **Down-chain (parent → child) is pushed** — `signalFollowUp` → `sessions.json` → the held Stop hook injects in ≤2 s. Reliable; never appears as wasted wall-clock.
* **Up-chain (child → parent) is pulled** — a child finishes and emits its sentinel, but the parent only notices by polling (a background long-poll, or a slow recommend-and-dispatch cycle). That poll is the dominant source of dead air: **17–48 % of three measured runs**, with cap-latency hits of 10–19 min per hop.

Root cause (grounded in `hook.js`): a session can wait two ways — an **async-wait defer** (a background `Bash`/`Monitor`/`ScheduleWakeup`; *not* holdable; harness re-invokes — a PULL) or a **holdable stop** (`DONE`/`PENDING` + `waitForFollowUps` → parks `AWAITING_FOLLOWUP`, dispatcher signals a follow-up in — a PUSH). The orchestrator waits on its **children** using the async-wait/poll mechanism — a category error. Children waiting for their next beat already use the holdable/push path correctly. This task makes the up-direction use the same push the down-direction already uses.

## The design (think network, not hierarchy)

Every session is the same thing: **hold-and-receive + emit-and-report.** A "leaf" only reports up; an "internal node" both signals down and reports up. The difference is which edges it has, not its code. An **event** is a session reaching a stopping point; **routing** is delivering that event along an edge as a follow-up.

Most of the machinery already exists and is reused:

| Piece | Status |
| -- | -- |
| **The edge** (who to notify) | EXISTS — every child dispatch is stamped `sessionId = <parent dispatch id>` |
| **The publish** (event detection) | EXISTS — `lib/dispatch-terminal.js` already detects `[done]`/`[failed]`/`[aborted]` in feedback; runner posts terminal markers |
| **The deliver** (push to a held session) | EXISTS — `resolveFollowUpTarget` returns `action:'signal'` for any `AWAITING_FOLLOWUP` session; injected in ≤2 s; role-agnostic (already universal) |
| **The hold + queue-when-busy** | LANDED — LIN-827 (`queueIfBusy`, extended hold) |
| **The subscription + auto-enqueue** | NEW (small, Harbour) — declare the edge at dispatch; on a child's terminal event, enqueue a follow-up addressed to the parent |
| **Autopilot adoption** | NEW — stop polling, trust the push |

## Locked design decisions (from the [LIN-824](https://linear.app/linearviewer/issue/LIN-824/research-agent-wait-latency-audit-where-does-the-wall-clock-go-when) discussion)

1. **The queue lives in Harbour**, reusing the existing dispatch queue. It already separates *peek* (`poll`) from *claim* (`take`) and items already carry their target (`followUpTo`). No new store.
2. **The runner gates** `take` **on local session-readiness.** (LANDED in LIN-827: `queueIfBusy` leaves a busy-target follow-up unclaimed instead of failing it; session-readiness knowledge stays in the runner — Harbour never learns the Claude session UUID.)
3. **Harbour is the source/router of the up-chain follow-up.** It already detects the child terminal; the new wire is "on terminal, enqueue a parent-addressed follow-up." The runner stays dumb.
4. **A subscription is also a liveness anchor.** Never reap a subscriber while it has a non-terminal subscribed child. **Deferred** past V1 — the extended + re-arming 60 min hold (LIN-827) covers the common case; the real anchor needs child-dispatch state and is sequenced with the parallel-execution track.
5. **Extend the hold budget** for subscribed waits — DONE in LIN-827 (~1 h). The `--resume` fallback covers anything past the cap, so this is tuning, not a correctness risk.
6. **Events that wake a parent are all terminal outcomes** — `[done]`, `[failed]`, `[aborted]`, and `[blocked]` (a failed/blocked child must wake its parent so it can react, not only a clean done).

## Phases

### Phase 1 — Harbour: subscription + auto-enqueue (the core)

* Add a **subscription declaration** at dispatch time (e.g. a `subscribe` flag): "route this child's terminal events to the dispatching parent." V1 scope = parent-subscribes-to-its-child (the edge is `child.sessionId`); model it so multiple/non-parent subscribers are a later additive step, not a rewrite.
* On detecting a child's terminal event (reuse `dispatch-terminal.js` `findTerminalFeedback`), **auto-enqueue a follow-up** addressed to the parent (`followUpTo = parent`, resolved via the `child.sessionId` edge), carrying the child's outcome (terminal summary + child issue/identifier link — Harbour already has this text), flagged `queueIfBusy: true` so it waits rather than fails if the parent is mid-judgment (the LIN-827 path).
* Pass `waitForFollowUps: true` on the orchestrator's kickoff dispatch so it parks holdable.
* Reuse the existing `signal` delivery path unchanged.
* **Acceptance:** a held parent receives a child's completion as an injected follow-up in seconds, with zero polling.

### Phase 2 — Autopilot adoption (mechanism-out, expectation-in)

The orchestrator pulls today because the **kickoff guide explicitly tells it to** — `lib/prompts/autopilot-kickoff.js` step 3 is a long-poll loop: `do { r = GET .../dispatch/{id}?wait=50 } while (!terminal(r))`. That loop keeps the agent actively running, so it never reaches a holdable stop. Setting `waitForFollowUps` alone does nothing while the guide still says "watch by polling."

* **Swap the watch procedure for the contract.** Replace step 3's poll loop with a short positive statement of what to expect: *after you dispatch a step you are subscribed to it; stop and stand by; when it reaches a terminal outcome (*`done`*/*`failed`*/*`blocked`*) you will be woken automatically with that outcome as a follow-up — do not poll, do not build your own watch loop, just resume your cross-check when it arrives.* Explain the **why** (so the agent trusts it and doesn't invent its own coordination), not a new procedure. No new "emit PENDING" instruction is needed — the hold is automatic once the agent stops without an outstanding async-wait.
* **Keep two judgments that remain the agent's job, not the runtime's:**
  * The **wedged-session ceiling** — the runtime pushes terminal *outcomes*, but a worker that goes silent without ever terminating still needs the agent's liveness nudge (~30 min of zero new activity → one-line liveness follow-up → re-dispatch or hand back). Keep this; just unwrap it from the poll loop.
  * **"**`done` **means go look, not finished"** — the step-4 cross-check (fetch `[evidence]`, confirm the deliverable exists, watch for `done`-while-still-waiting-on-CI) is unchanged.
* **Acceptance:** an epic run shows no orchestrator long-poll episodes; inter-beat latency is at the push floor.

## Validation

Run-and-watch is the acceptance: fire a stepper autopilot at real to-do work and observe. If it works — mark done, and we've both validated the change and shipped whatever the run landed. If it hangs or wrinkles, we learn the exact failure on real evidence and the work still gets done (a hang falls back to the existing reaper/resume net). The [LIN-824](https://linear.app/linearviewer/issue/LIN-824/research-agent-wait-latency-audit-where-does-the-wall-clock-go-when) dead-air harness (`deadair2.py`) is a **post-hoc confirmation** of the up-chain dead-air collapse vs the 17 % baseline, not a gate to pass first. An open question worth watching: whether the agent *naturally* reads "you'll be notified" and stands by, vs. defaulting to invent-a-loop — the prompt can't fully guarantee it; a real run reveals it.

## Out of scope (named, deliberate)

* **Parallel execution** of children — a separate planned track. This task makes the comms reliable so parallel can build on it; it does not implement fan-out.
* **The true liveness anchor** (decision #4) — deferred to the parallel track; the 60 min re-arming hold covers V1.
* **The orchestrator loop-death** ([LIN-824](https://linear.app/linearviewer/issue/LIN-824/research-agent-wait-latency-audit-where-does-the-wall-clock-go-when) finding #3: agent loop stalling at `stop_reason: tool_use`) — a separate agent-liveness/nudge-before-reap concern.
* **The post-done hold tail** — not a concern; lazy session reaping covers it.

## Testing & monitoring

* Keep the **pure-core pattern**: the new subscribe / auto-enqueue logic in Harbour should be pure functions with unit tests, effects at the edges — mirroring `dispatch-terminal.js` and the LIN-827 runner predicates.
* **Both-paths note:** this is dispatch/coordination wiring, not prompt-recommendation behaviour, so the two-prompt-paths parity rule does not apply. The autopilot-guide change is a single edit to `lib/prompts/autopilot-kickoff.js` (and the operating manual if it echoes the poll loop).

---

*Origin:* [LIN-824](https://linear.app/linearviewer/issue/LIN-824/research-agent-wait-latency-audit-where-does-the-wall-clock-go-when) *(research). Runner half:* [LIN-827](https://linear.app/linearviewer/issue/LIN-827) *(landed).*

issue.title: Add a copy-to-clipboard button to each proxy-token row
issue.description:
## Implementation Plan

1. In `lib/render-proxy.js`, add a small copy button to each token row, stamped with a `data-token` attribute carrying the token value.
2. In `public/proxy.js`, wire a click handler that reads `data-token`, writes it via `navigator.clipboard.writeText`, and flips the button label to `copied` for ~1s.

Both changes land together in one PR — the button is dead markup without the handler, and the handler has nothing to bind without the button, so there is one cohesive deliverable and one close-out. Tests: one unit assertion that the rendered row contains the copy button with its `data-token`.

Single focused surface (the proxy token page); no phases, no independently-landable parts.
